text.p: British chemicals group Hickson International Plc said on Thursday it was now fully on the road to recovery from its 1995 profits collapse.
"We feel we have made a lot of progress and we are out of hospital and back to being a normal operating company," chief executive David Wilbraham told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Earlier Hickson announced the latest in a string of disposals aimed at cutting debts and focusing on core businesses in protective chemicals and coatings, agrochemicals and pigments.

News of the sale of the Irish-based drug intermediates maker PharmaChem to Warner-Lambert Co for 28.5 million stg pushed the group's share price up by more than 10 percent in afternoon trading to 79 pence.
This marks a jump of 58 percent from a low of 50 pence touched in January, but is still well below the two-year peak of 135 pence in May 1995.
In November Hickson announced the sale of another major part of its business, the surfactants operation Hickson Manro, for 26.5 million stg.
Wilbraham said the sales had allowed the company to meet obligations to its bankers, who took control of assets when the business nose-dived, and to bring gearing down to around 27 percent.
Following completion, the group's net debt would be around 30 million stg compared with a peak of 103.4 million stg in November 1995, Hickson said.
The company was now a "hell of a sight different," said Wilbraham, who was brought in to take control of the struggling operation.

"In November 1995 we had a profits collapse, gearing over 100 percent, the banks moved in to take control of assets and the chief executive was turfed out. Now we have brought gearing down to below 30 percent, turned the businesses round so they are now performing...and showing a profit trend that is rising," he told Reuters.
Wilbraham said other disposals were possible, but only if there was "a good business reason for it."
"We are not expecting anything major," he said.
Restoration of the dividend, which has not been paid since 1995, was "something we will now look at", he added, but would not be drawn on timing.

The chief executive said the company had succeeded in rebalancing its portfolio of businesses and getting rid of excessive debt. He forecast growth in the group's timber treatment operations, where Hickson is number one worldwide, led by a new product in the U.S. for renovating wooden communication and electricity poles and protecting decks, or terraces, on houses.
While wood and furniture coating and treatment markets were strong in the U.S, Wilbraham said continental Europe was "particularly flat."
"What we are doing is growing new markets by expanding into eastern Europe and the Far East," he said.
The biggest growth area would be the Hickson & Welch business, notably in the increasingly strong agrochemical sector, where Hickson's customers include major players like E.I Du Pont de Nemours.
Wilbraham said the company would be investing to expand production in this area.
